Jeffrey,
First quickly, thanks for (probably without having to think about it) giving so much of yourself for the benefit of others. Many don;t connect the work done by you and others like to to really what it is: Selfless giving. (but your no saint from what I hear,,,,, Just kidding)…
Allow me to hijack this thread for one moment in time. If it gets legs you decide where to let it run.
********
This is a first set of ideas that I am working into a far more concise paper so pardon the usual early draft issues. The ideas are mostly here however.
I am sure if people are here they will like the content and I think others can benefit before I will have time to polish. Or this may be useless… Fair warning (grin).
First the stage;
Keep in mind in all cases except where stated I refer only to the vast majority in corporate American business. Large business. I am not qualifies nearly as much to be as confident in these statement say for German firms.
It’s irrelevant as I will discuss how this is not about technology (at least not today). Let say you are like me as someone who without pause will discuss the implementation of single responsibility entity classes with injected (via IoC containers) DAO concerned/interface defined add-in modules (yes AppDomain isolated and run-time swappable even wow!) to vendor ORM implementations that resolve our contracts.
Who cares. It’s fun and it’s great money and it’s a great sound bite. WE must face the fact that regardless of your technical merit it’s about the domain. Hapilly if your technically amazing that will be aligned under most circumstances, even broken ones.
This is not about us. This is for people who are not there. This is for people with real lives but who care deeply for optimization. They will eclipse our value add if we do not also change in the next years I assert.
Said more directly we can deliver exponential earth shattering results if an ORGANIZATION ALLOWS US TO. Most will not regardless of any merit on ANY METRIC you claim if all you have is IT benefit (scope, time, quality, cost, predictability, ability to react via feedback loopsm etc).
It will get attention but not real attention from the majority (remember my qualification).
This post could be called ‘the last five years of my life’ or ‘Drowning on-shore surrounded by lifeguards distracted’. Indeed I had the skills at the right time and I did all the right work and indeed had amazing successes by my standards and all the IT organizations standards.
Once you understand how very large business defines this you realize it was nothing and nobody truly important likely even heard about it.
So again in other words: It is likely irrelevant on any ‘grand level’ how well we do this knowing ORM just gets us to domain-driven.
Well how DO we move to the big-leagues. We’ve always known. Nothing is new. Only the assumed means of how we will get these. And history has proven we cannot do it but I think we will this time.
I think we are about to explode in good ways that will destroy careers and make a new generation of CTO-CEO promotions the norm. This is what I have been waiting for but did not dare to expect.
But I’ll likely be retired when it is real. Perhaps not. Who knows. Knowing how hard this is NOW and believe me I use everything I can to make it easier, it is not about technology.
Once it hits you that people stop this, you must give up an attempt to control. The meaning or mastery in ORM just not what it used it be,.
Again, think 80% GDP here. This is how our economy works more then not. This segment (the main segment really) really has no idea what to do with people like us or even who want to be like us for the most part,
